topic: The Most Beautiful Equation: Euler's Formula and the Magic of e^(πi) = -1
target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students with basic knowledge of algebra and trigonometry.

sections.title: The Grand Introduction: A Meeting of Giants
lecture_lines: Mathematics holds a secret that unites its greatest constants.
Meet zero, one, pi, e, and the imaginary i.
They seem unrelated, like stars in different galaxies.
Yet, one elegant formula binds them all together perfectly.
Today, we uncover the magic of Euler’s Identity.
animations: A soft white (#FFFFFF) glow appears in the center of a black (#000000) screen.
The numbers 0 (white #FFFFFF), 1 (white #FFFFFF), pi (orange #FFA500), e (green #00FF00), and i (blue #0000FF) appear around the glow.
The five symbols drift apart toward the corners of the screen like distant stars.
The symbols fly back to the center, beginning to assemble into the equation e^(pi*i) + 1 = 0.
The complete equation e^(pi*i) + 1 = 0 appears in bold gold (#FFD700) and scales up slightly.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Hidden Power of 'i'
lecture_lines: Beyond square roots, i is a master of rotation.
Multiplying by i turns any number ninety degrees left.
It transforms simple algebra into dynamic geometric motion.
animations: A horizontal white (#FFFFFF) line appears with a point at (1,0). The symbol 'i' appears in the top corner.

A vector [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg] from the origin to (1,0) rotates 90 degrees counter-clockwise to point at (0,1). The point (0,1) is labeled 'i' in light blue (#ADD8E6).
The vector [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg] rotates another 90 degrees to point at (-1,0), showing the transition from algebra to geometry.

sections.title: The Growth Engine: What is 'e'?
lecture_lines: The constant e represents the spirit of continuous growth.
Usually, e pushes us along the real number line.
But what if our growth rate is purely imaginary?
animations: The letter 'e' appears in light green (#90EE90) in the center, pulsing slightly, accompanied by an engine icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/engine.svg] to represent its role as the engine of growth.
A point on a horizontal line moves from 1 towards the right, accelerating to show exponential growth.
The growth direction arrow rotates 90 degrees upward and changes to light blue (#ADD8E6) to represent imaginary growth.

sections.title: Euler’s Formula: Rotation in Disguise
lecture_lines: Raising e to an imaginary power changes everything.
Instead of growing larger, we start to turn sideways.
This sideways growth traces a path around a circle.
Euler’s formula maps this rotation using sine and cosine.
It reveals that complex exponentials are actually circular motions.
animations: The expression e^(ix) appears at the top in white (#FFFFFF).
A vector starts at (1,0) on a 2D plane and begins rotating counter-clockwise.
As the vector rotates, it draws a yellow (#FFFF00) circle of radius 1.
The formula e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x) appears below, with 'cos' in red (#FF0000) and 'sin' in blue (#0000FF).
The vector continues to spin around the circle, demonstrating continuous circular motion.

sections.title: The Journey of π: Reaching the Destination
lecture_lines: Now, let our rotation travel a distance of pi.
Pi radians represents exactly half a trip around.
We land precisely at negative one on the axis.
animations: The formula e^(ix) changes to e^(pi*i) in the center of the screen.
On a unit circle [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/unit.svg], a point moves from the rightmost edge (1,0) exactly halfway around to the leftmost edge (-1,0).
The point at (-1,0) flashes and the number -1 appears in white (#FFFFFF) next to it.

sections.title: The Final Synthesis: e^(πi) + 1 = 0
lecture_lines: e to the pi i equals negative one.
By adding one, we reach the balance of zero.
All five fundamental constants unified in a single line.
It is the most beautiful equation in all mathematics.
A perfect bridge between geometry, calculus, and algebra.
